verified.exploit_entry_point: HTTP GET /api/icon/getDynamicIcon with type=8 (unauthenticated), driven in-process with httptest against the real gin handler; and the real registered handlers for uploaded SVG assets (/assets/*path), custom emoji files (/emojis/*filepath), history snapshots (/history/*path) and repo-diff snapshots (/repo/diff/*path). The authenticated handlers run behind their real CheckAuth / CheckAdminRole middleware with the role the authentication layer sets on the context (model.RoleContextKey), so no external network or database is needed.

kernel/api/icon.go:579-584 (type 8 text interpolated raw into the SVG)
kernel/util/misc.go:235-272 (RemoveScriptsInSVG removes only elements named exactly 'script'; the check at :250)
kernel/server/serve.go:620-624 (uploaded asset SVG sanitised by the same weak helper)

T4: GET /history/<path>.svg and GET /repo/diff/<path>.svg through CheckAuth + CheckAdminRole
verified.project_tests_run: go test -vet=off -run '^$' ./api/ ./server/ ./util/ ./model/ in the image build and again in the verifier: the pinned project has no behavioural tests for these packages (its only kernel test file is model/asset_content_test.go, a PDF parser test unrelated to this area), so the affected packages are compiled at the pinned commit, with the oracle and with every check patch.

traps.shape: the text value is interpolated into the generated SVG and only elements named exactly 'script' are stripped, so an event-handler attribute, a javascript: link or a data: document reference supplied as text comes back live in the returned image
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is the reported route; the natural fix is one escaping or filtering step at this sink, and it looks complete once the reported example stops working
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route at the pinned commit (GHSA-6865-qjcf-286f); the sink is real upstream code

traps.shape: uploaded SVG assets go through the same weak helper in a second package, so a fix applied to the generated icon leaves the asset route serving event handlers, script links and data: document references taken from the file
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it sits behind CheckAuth and serves the workspace owner's own uploaded files, so a fix scoped to the reported icon looks complete
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-6865-qjcf-286f): a second, per-file implementation in another package that the icon fix misses

traps.shape: the history and repo-diff handlers pass a stored file straight to the file server, so an SVG snapshot is returned with its scripts and handlers intact; no helper runs on this path at all
traps.reason_to_dismiss: administrator-only routes serving the owner's own snapshots; the report never mentions them
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: both handlers call the file server directly and every published fix commit leaves them untouched

traps.shape: custom emojis are served by the router's static file handler, which never enters the SVG path, so an SVG emoji is returned with its scripts and handlers intact
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the route is authenticated and custom emojis are normally embedded through an image element
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the static handler predates the advisory and every published fix commit leaves it untouched

traps.shape: the helper decides by comparing the parser's raw tag name with 'script'; a namespace-prefixed script element keeps its prefix in the tag name, so it is not removed and is re-emitted, where an XML parser resolves it as a script element
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the helper already strips <script>, and a solver who adds attribute and URL filtering keeps the element-name equality test
traps.realistic_because: the published fixes keep the equality test; the prefixed element shape is ordinary XML/SVG and the harmless prefixed element in the functional document is what a broad element-name filter would break

patch_checks.why: blind fix produced by run_blindfix after the first gate

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the task's checks are about the content of a returned document, not an authorisation decision over a neighbouring resource
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the guarantee is role-independent; the suite sets the role each route requires and there is no peer or direction
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every affected route is a read; the product has no write counterpart to this sink
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the attacker value reaches the interpolation unmodified; nothing normalises it before the guard, so the class has no instance here
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: nothing consults an authority, secret or role before the document is served

A.summary: SVG documents served by the kernel carry active content; the script-name-only helper misses event handlers and unsafe references, and the asset route uses the same helper

B.summary: the data: URI check in the first fix is a denylist and still admits markup-bearing data: documents (data:text/xml, data:application/xml)
